topIssues.title: Kona and op-node can disagree on brotli channels
topIssues.author: kevin-valerio
topIssues.body:
## Bugs description
This issue actually contains two distinct bugs that can cause divergence between Kona and op-node for brotli-compressed channels.

- Bug 1: `decompress_brotli` can return `Ok()` even when brotli decompression did **not** reach `ResultSuccess`.
- Bug 2: Kona selects brotli based on the leading version byte and only later gates Fjord using `batch.timestamp`. op-node gates brotli **up front** using the L1 inclusion context (`isFjord`).

If a system uses Kona in a fault proof program / dispute game, these divergences can lead to incorrect outputs becoming accepted on Kona, while being refused on op-node. 

### `decompress_brotli` returns `Ok()` without requiring `ResultSuccess`

`decompress_brotli` loops only while the decoder returns `NeedsMoreOutput`. If the decoder returns `NeedsMoreInput` or `ResultFailure`, the loop stops and the function still returns `Ok(output_truncated_to_written_bytes)`.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/brotli.rs#L44-L73

Kona can treat invalid or truncated brotli as "valid decompressed bytes" (even if potentially empty), returning `Ok(vec![])` or `Ok(partial_bytes)`. The function only errors when the output would exceed `max_rlp_bytes_per_channel` (`BatchTooLarge`).

This is a divergence against op-node behavior that streams decompression through `brotli.NewReader(...)` and propagate errors during RLP decode if the brotli stream is truncated or invalid.

###  Fjord brotli gating is checked too late and uses a different time basis
In Kona, `BatchReader::decompress` decides "this is brotli" from the first byte (`CHANNEL_VERSION_BROTLI == 1`) and then decompresses the rest. `BatchReader::next_batch` only rejects brotli *after* decoding a batch, by checking Fjord using `cfg.is_fjord_active(batch.timestamp())`.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/reader.rs#L95-L98


https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/rust/kona/crates/protocol/protocol/src/batch/reader.rs#L117-L120

However, in op-node, brotli is gated **up front** using the L1 inclusion context (`isFjord`). If it’s not Fjord, op-node rejects brotli immediately.

https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/2460e59c372921d96eed4a204825fef98ba67bc8/op-node/rollup/derive/channel.go#L193-L197

Kona and op-node can disagree on whether brotli is acceptable around Fjord, because Kona’s check is based on **`batch.timestamp()` (L2 data)** and happens **after** decompression+decode, while op-node’s check is based on the **L1 inclusion context** and happens **before** setting up the brotli reader.
 
### Risk for the truncated brotli stream being accepted by Kona (bug 1)
A buggy authorized batch submitter sends an L1 batch inbox transaction whose channel starts with the brotli version byte `0x01`. An actor crafts a brotli stream that starts decompressing into a valid RLP-encoded batch, then truncates the brotli data so the decoder ends in `NeedsMoreInput` (not `ResultSuccess`). `op-node` brotli is streamed via `brotli.NewReader`, and the RLP decode fails due to invalid decompression. Kona `decompress_brotli` returns `Ok(partial_bytes)` and the batch decode can succeed from those bytes. Kona derives a different output than op-node. 

### Risk for pre-Fjord inclusion but post-Fjord batch timestamp (bug 2)
Assume `fjord_time = 2_000`. An actor submits a brotli channel (first byte `0x01`) in an L1 inclusion context with `origin.timestamp = 1_999` (pre-Fjord). The decoded batch inside the channel uses `batch.timestamp = 2_000` (Fjord-active by timestamp). `op-node`'s `isFjord == false` based on L1 inclusion context, so brotli is rejected immediately. 

However brotli decompression runs, the batch is decoded, and the Fjord check uses `cfg.is_fjord_active(batch.timestamp()) == true`, so the batch can be accepted. Kona accepts brotli data that op-node rejects, again creating derivation divergence risk.

### Fix for the first bug
Change `decompress_brotli` to return an error unless `BrotliDecompressStream()` reaches `BrotliResult::ResultSuccess`. Handle `NeedsMoreInput` and `ResultFailure` as errors, not as "success with partial output".

### Fix for the second bug
Gate brotli before decompression using the L1 inclusion context, as op-node’s `isFjord` is doing. Pass an `is_fjord`/`origin_timestamp` decision into the Kona `BatchReader` and reject brotli channels pre-Fjord.

## Author notes
This bug was initially reported in Immunefi but closed since considered as out-of-scope. These bugs were found using a differential fuzzing approach and [gosentry](https://github.com/kevin-valerio/gosentry).

topIssues.title: Replace supervisor RPC namespace with interop filter namespace
topIssues.author: karlfloersch
topIssues.body:
## Summary

The supervisor is being removed. The interop filter currently registers itself under the `supervisor` RPC namespace for backwards compatibility, but it should have its own dedicated namespace.

## Current State

**op-supervisor** (`op-supervisor/supervisor/service.go`) registers the `supervisor` RPC namespace with the full `SupervisorQueryAPI`:
- `supervisor_checkAccessList`, `supervisor_crossDerivedToSource`, `supervisor_localUnsafe`, `supervisor_localSafe`, `supervisor_crossSafe`, `supervisor_finalized`, `supervisor_finalizedL1`, `supervisor_superRootAtTimestamp`, `supervisor_allSafeDerivedAt`, `supervisor_syncStatus`

**op-interop-filter** (`op-interop-filter/filter/service.go`) also registers the `supervisor` namespace but only implements `CheckAccessList`:
```go
server.AddAPI(rpc.API{
    Namespace:     "supervisor",
    Service:       &QueryFrontend{backend: s.backend},
    Authenticated: false,
})
```

This lets op-node's `SupervisorClient` (`op-service/sources/supervisor_client.go`) call `supervisor_checkAccessList` against the interop filter without knowing the difference — but it's a backwards compat hack.

## Proposed Changes

1. Delete the `supervisor` RPC namespace (as part of removing op-supervisor)
2. Add a new RPC namespace for the interop filter (e.g. `interop` or `interop_filter`)
3. Update op-node's client to call the new namespace (e.g. `interop_checkAccessList` instead of `supervisor_checkAccessList`)
4. Clean up the `SupervisorQueryAPI` interface in `op-service/apis/supervisor.go` — the interop filter only needs `CheckAccessList`, not the full 9-method interface

## Motivation

- The supervisor is being deleted — keeping its namespace around is confusing
- Two services sharing the same RPC namespace with different implementations is a source of bugs
- The interop filter only implements 1 of 9 supervisor query methods — it deserves its own clean interface

topIssues.author: pauldowman
topIssues.body:
In order to delete op-supervisor, we still have a number of op-e2e tests in super_test.go that need to be migrated to op-acceptance-tests. The remaining tests are the ones that exercise playing out a dispute game on chain.

topIssues.title: [flake] TestSupernodeInterop_SafeHeadProgression — EL safe label race with CL cross-safe
topIssues.author: ajsutton
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Tracking flake observed in pipeline 125516.

## Failure

Job: https://app.circleci.com/pipelines/github/ethereum-optimism/optimism/125516/workflows/c482ad78-69f5-4051-ad85-f2ce1adcf4af/jobs/5062361

```
assertions.go:387:
    Error Trace: op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/interop/head_progression_test.go:89
    Error:       "9" is not greater than or equal to "10"
    Test:        TestSupernodeInterop_SafeHeadProgression
--- FAIL: TestSupernodeInterop_SafeHeadProgression (31.97s)
```

## Suspected root cause (to be confirmed by fix agent)

After `dsl.CheckAll(...)` confirms the CL reached `CrossSafe = finalTargetBlockNum (10)`, the test immediately reads the EL safe label via `sys.L2ELA.BlockRefByLabel(eth.Safe)` and asserts it is `>= 10`. The EL safe label is updated asynchronously through the engine API forkchoice flow, so there is a small window where the CL has marked the block cross-safe but the EL `safe` label still trails by one block.

Log evidence from the failing run:
- `INFO l2_cl.go:283 Chain advanced name=sequencer chain=902 label=safe target=10 target=10` at `23:49:26.233`
- Assertion fired at `23:49:26.242` with `safeA.Number == 9`

## Fix direction

Replace the immediate EL label read at lines 87–90 (and likely similar reads later in the test) with a polling wait (e.g. `ReachedFn` or equivalent helper) that waits for the EL safe label to catch up to `finalTargetBlockNum` before asserting.

A fix PR is in progress.

topPRs.title: feat(contracts-bedrock): add feature flag registry and drift check
topPRs.author: lumoswiz
topPRs.body:
**Description**

Adds `packages/contracts-bedrock/feature-flags.yaml` as the feature flag registry and `go run ./scripts/checks/feature-flags` as a strict drift check.

How this addresses #20340:

- Single source of truth: the registry now owns feature names, feature type (`dev` / `sys`), lifecycle, dependency rules, exclusion rules, and supported CI matrix rows.
- Mechanical drift detection: the checker fails when the registry diverges from Solidity feature definitions/wiring, Go dev-feature definitions, hardcoded-on dev-feature branches, or CircleCI's `system_features.default` / `features_matrix`.
- Existing flags are backfilled: the registry covers current dev and sys flags, and this PR fixes the pre-existing `ETH_LOCKBOX` / `INTEROP` drift so the check can run strictly with no allowlist.

The backfill adds `sysFeatureEthLockbox()` and `sysFeatureInterop()` readers in `Config.sol`, adds the missing `Features.INTEROP` branch in `FeatureFlags.getFeatureName`, applies both sys features in `CommonTest.sol`, and expands CircleCI's feature matrix with `[ETH_LOCKBOX]` and `[OPTIMISM_PORTAL_INTEROP, ETH_LOCKBOX, INTEROP]`.

The check runs in `contracts-bedrock-checks-fast` via `checks.yaml`. A standalone `feature-flags-sync-check` job also covers PRs that only touch `op-core/devfeatures/` or `.circleci/` and would otherwise bypass contracts path gating.

**Tests**

- `mise exec -- go test ./scripts/checks/feature-flags`
- `mise exec -- go run ./scripts/checks/feature-flags`
- `mise exec -- just check-fast`
- `.circleci/scripts/test-decision-tree.sh`
- Manual drift perturbations against the real tree for missing/extra registry, Solidity, Go, and CircleCI entries, plus invalid/missing matrix rows. Each failed nonzero with an actionable error and reverted byte-clean.

**Additional context**

This PR uses enforcement rather than codegen. That satisfies the issue's "codegen, consistency check, or equivalent" path for drift detection, but it does not fully implement the strongest version of "adding a new flag requires editing one location." Adding a flag still requires updating the runtime surfaces that actually define or consume it; the registry is the source of truth, and CI fails if those edits do not match.

If reviewers prefer generation, the next step would be to extend the registry schema with generated constants/metadata and render the Solidity, Go, and/or CircleCI surfaces from it.

**Metadata**

Closes #20340

topPRs.title: feat(op-supernode): rework interop activity startup
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
Replaces the EL-finalized-head cold-start heuristic with a deterministic verifiedDB-resume / SafeDB-first-entry model.

## Why

The previous startup logic was a tangle:
- `resolveFirstVerifiableTimestamp` used EL finalized head as the cold-start origin — the wrong signal (EL's view of finality, not proof that derivation has run).
- A retry loop conflated transient EL not-ready with permanent SafeDB gaps.
- Backfill ran before deciding the verification start timestamp.
- `firstVerifiableTimestamp` re-derived its value lazily, sometimes with I/O, from RPC handlers.

## What changed

- **Resume always wins.** Any committed `verifiedDB` entry resumes at `LastTimestamp+1` without consulting SafeDB or chain RPCs.
- **Cold start** waits for every chain to record a first SafeDB entry, then sets `verificationStartTimestamp = max(activationTimestamp, max first-safe-head timestamp)`. Wall-clock time is never consulted.
- **Backfill** clamps lower bound to `max(activation, per-chain genesis, verificationStart - depth)`. Hard fails if any chain can't serve the range. `reconcileLogsDBTail` runs only during cold-start backfill.
- **Start** splits into a fast init + stateful main loop. The loop drives both cold-start init and `progressAndRecord`, so `Start` never blocks on multi-day EL sync waits. Per-iteration backoff, cancellation, and observability come for free.
- **`firstVerifiableTimestamp`** is now a synchronous accessor; RPC handlers return `ErrNotStarted` until init completes.

New API surface:
- `SafeDBReader.FirstEntry` (op-node) → `VirtualNode.FirstSafeHeadEntry` → `ChainContainer.FirstSafeHeadTimestamp`. Returns `ErrSafeDBEmpty` during cold-start wait.

## Tests

- New `startup_test.go` covers `fastInit` resume / cold-start, the `advanceColdStartInit` state machine, cold-start backfill no-op paths, per-chain genesis clamp, and RPC `ErrNotStarted` semantics.
- Deleted `log_backfill_test.go` and the obsolete EL-finalized-head startup tests in `interop_test.go` — replaced by the above.
- End-to-end resync acceptance tests (post- and pre-activation, with/without EL data wipe) are tracked as follow-up work, not included here.

topPRs.title: op-reth: try paradigmxyz/reth#24159 FCU backfill-target patch
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
Bumps the monorepo reth dependency to the head of paradigmxyz/reth#24159 (commit `e8c29c98`) so we can try out the FCU backfill-target change in op-reth.

The new rev is rebased on a newer reth main than the previously pinned `88505c7f`, so this PR also adapts op-reth to upstream API changes that came along for the ride:

- `FullConsensus::validate_block_post_execution`: new `block_access_list_hash: Option<B256>` param (ignored on OP — no BAL yet)
- `PayloadTypes::block_to_payload`: new `bal: Option<Bytes>` param
- `PayloadTypes::ExecutionData`: now requires `From<Self::BuiltPayload>` — added impls for `OpExecData` and the `CustomExecutionData` example
- `BlockAssemblerInput::new`: new 9th arg `Option<B256>` (BAL hash)
- `BlockBuilderOutcome`: new `block_access_list` field destructured and ignored
- `BuiltPayloadExecutedBlock.{hashed_state,trie_updates}`: now plain `Arc<...>` (no `Either` wrapping) — dropped the `either` dep from `reth-optimism-payload-builder`
- `OpEngineApi`: `Provider` bound now needs `BalProvider`
- Tests: `discv5_port`/`discv5_port_ipv6` are now `Option<u16>`

Verified locally: `cargo check --workspace --tests` and `cargo build -p op-reth` succeed; `cargo +nightly fmt --check` clean.

Draft because the underlying reth PR (#24159) is itself unmerged — this should not land until that upstream PR merges and we can bump to a clean rev. Until then this is purely for evaluating the FCU behavior change end-to-end in op-reth.
